title: Tear down a background loop + schedule after a handoff, then stay responsive

turns.prompt: Start a long background loop with a subagent: every 15 seconds for the next 30 minutes append the current UTC time to {D}/loop.log. Also create a scheduled job (routine) that runs every minute and appends the word tick to {D}/sched.log. Reply as soon as both are set up.
Quick check before I decide anything: what exactly is running right now — is the loop still appending, and does the scheduled job exist?
turns.verify: n=$(test -f {D}/loop.log && grep -c . {D}/loop.log || echo 0); p=$(pgrep -af 'loop.sh|lt-b4-teardown' | grep -vE 'prime-agent|rlm.repl|pgrep' | wc -l); echo "SHOW loop_lines=$n loop_procs=$p"; if [ $n -ge 2 ]; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL: loop never ran; fi

rubric.criteria: Judge the reply text only (the loop and the routine are verified programmatically). The reply gives a real status: loop running / how far, schedule exists; it does not stall or ask the user what to do.

turns.prompt: Tear everything down now: stop the loop and kill any process behind it, delete the scheduled job, and confirm when nothing is running any more.
turns.verify: m1=$(stat -c %Y {D}/loop.log 2>/dev/null || echo 0); sleep 35; m2=$(stat -c %Y {D}/loop.log 2>/dev/null || echo 0); p=$(pgrep -af 'lt-b4-teardown' | grep -vE 'prime-agent|rlm.repl|pgrep' | wc -l); echo "SHOW loop_mtime_moved=$([ $m1 != $m2 ] && echo yes || echo no) loop_procs=$p"; if [ $m1 = $m2 ] && [ $p -eq 0 ]; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL: loop still alive; fi

regression: Doug teardown incident 2026-10-22 13:44 CR (owner bc-d117b386); #2258 (run 12: the teardown's follow-on job ended 'interrupted / box restart' at 00:58:24 and the turn never confirmed, though the routine was deleted and the loop killed)
